where: Section 1 and Section 2 (with the Figure note and Q1)
problem: The loop polarity as wired cannot oscillate; it latches. With R1 from the non-inverting input to ground and R2 from the output to the non-inverting input, the Schmitt trigger trips when the voltage on its inverting input rises past +βVsat, so it is an inverting stage from the triangle to the square. The integrator is also inverting (vout = −(1/RC)∫vin dt). Two inversions make the loop positive feedback: with the square at +Vsat the ramp falls, so the ramp can never climb to +βVsat, and the circuit sits at a rail. The text even says the ramp rises while the square is high ('When the ramp crosses +βVsat the comparator flips'), which an inverting integrator cannot do.
fix: Make the loop net negative feedback by reversing one inversion. Option (a), keeps every number: move the divider to the inverting input (R1 from the inverting input to ground, R2 from the output to the inverting input) and connect the integrator output directly to the non-inverting input. Thresholds stay ±βVsat with β = R1/(R1+R2) and f = 1/(4βRC), so ±4 V, 7.5 kHz and 20 % duty all stand. Then Section 1 must read: the output stays at +Vsat while the ramp is above +βVsat, and drops to −Vsat when the ramp falls below +βVsat. Option (b): keep the wiring and make the integrator non-inverting, vout = +(1/RC)∫vin dt; then the existing sentences in Sections 1 and 2 read correctly and all numbers stand. Whichever option is used, Q1's answer must describe the same wiring.

problem: The diode names and the resistor names do not match. 'Diode A conducts while the square is at +Vsat' means the resistance on that path is the falling-path resistance, because the integrator inverts. The formula then defines RA as the resistance on the rising path. A student will pair diode A with RA and get the duty cycle upside down.
fix: Drop the A/B labels, or say: the diode that conducts while the square is at −Vsat sets the rising-path resistance RA; the other diode, which conducts while the square is at +Vsat, sets the falling-path resistance RB. Then duty = RA/(RA + RB).

problem: The note gives thresholds ±4 V and β = 1/3 but never states Vsat, so a reader cannot check that βVsat = 4 V; the 12 V supply appears only in the worked example.
fix: Add 'Vsat = ±12 V' to the Schmitt trigger node note, so ±βVsat = ±4 V can be checked from the figure alone.
